all.text: At this latitude, the Earth's spin carries the ship east at about 910 mph, whatever the captain is doing.
The sun reaches its highest point here about 55 minutes after it does in Southampton.
Drill straight through the Earth from here and you'd surface at 28.1°S, 164.8°E, about 1,340 km from Auckland.
This far north, they're roughly level with Kathmandu, even though it's a world away.
The seabed is roughly 1,723 m below the ship, which is about 5.2 Eiffel Towers stacked up.
